word.name: element-fits-schema
word.title: Element Fits Schema
word.description: An element's JSON fits the JSON schema of each concept it belongs to.

graphRule.name: element-fits-schema
graphRule.says: an element's JSON fits the JSON schema of each concept it belongs to. This is BIBLE §10's rule 4, "Elements MUST validate against their concept's JSON Schema", and the owner's D9: each node is an element of at least one concept, and must validate against the format that concept expects. A node belongs to every concept whose class thread reaches it (rule 3), so an element in a set that two concepts' class threads reach has two schemas to fit. A schema is read as the derive step reads it (`src/lib/derivers/word.js`): the JSON schema node's `jsonSchema` section, its `$schema` dropped, checked with ajv's defaults, which read draft-07's keywords. So this rule and the derive step's `parentJsonSchemas` give one verdict.
graphRule.kind: a graph rule, about the owner's and the admins' own element writes (D4). As a check it judges every element by where it came from (D15): an element an import brought in is reported, never refused.
graphRule.refusesOrReports:
it refuses the write, before anything changes:
- `invalid-fields` (400) when the element's JSON doesn't fit the concept's schema. The refusal lists every problem, each naming the field and what is wrong: a required field left out, a value of the wrong type, a value the schema doesn't allow, a field the schema doesn't take. It names at most twenty, then how many more. No value is made up for a field left out;
- `no-schema` (409) when the concept's schema is missing, can't be read, or doesn't compile, so nothing could be checked. The refusal says why.

An element in a set may join other concepts too. The write reports whether its JSON fits each of their schemas, and doesn't refuse for them: giving the element their sections is `graph add-to-concept` (A10.22).
graphRule.check: the same `violations` over a set of elements, each as `{ node }`, names each element and each concept whose schema it doesn't fit, and each concept with no schema to check against; as `{ node, concept }` it judges against the one named. An element whose JSON can't be read is named once. `rules check` (A10.31) will run it over the graph. The property operations (A10.18) will run it over a concept's elements after its schema changes, reporting only.
graphRule.repair: none yet. `graph update-node` (A10.21) changes an element's fields, and `graph add-to-concept` (A10.22) gives it another concept's section.
graphRule.enforcedBy: the guard of `graph create-element`, run in its write once it has taken the lock on the concept's header and built the element's JSON, since that JSON comes from the graph. The rule's code is in `src/operations/rules/element-fits-schema.js`. The check it uses is in `src/operations/catalog/graph/_schemas.js`, which `graph update-node`, `graph add-to-concept` and the property operations will call too. Built in story graph-operations-first-slice #20 (ADR graph-operations-first-slice/0020).
